How do I feel when playing SotM? Let's see.

Sotm is my well-worn baseball cap. It sits comfortably on my head, putting some pressure on, but I feel like I'm missing something if it's not there.

SotM is the zebra to my lion. I stalk it, looking for signs of weakness. When the moment is right, I strike, ripping bloody chunks off for the rest of my pack to devour.

SotM is a rod of plutonium. In 88 years, it will be only halfway through its lifespan on my table. But it's dangerous. It gets into my system, changing me at the most basic level.

After much mental debate, I think I have settled on Australia.  Prefereably urban approximate (I wouldn't want to end up in some desert).  The language is the easiest non American language to understand, and it seems to be a rather nice place.  Japan would be nice, if not due to the overlap between a place having way to many people, and a place having not enough going on such that it is boring (i.e. every place that is not too popular for me would likely be fairly boring, and any place that's not fairly boring to me would be too popular, and some places would be too popular and boring at the same time)(note that I'm using the definition of popular to mean number of people, not the common definition used today to indicate wide admiration).  Even though China seems to be an obvious choice for me, I don't really like the political state to the point that I likely wouldn't choose it out of a list (though I wouldn't be completely against a short trip, possibly in one of the "Free Trade Zones" of Shanghai).  A Pacific island might be fun too.

Now is the hard part... I must pretend to have enough interest to ask another person something and to actually care about the response...

posts.name: Rabit
posts.cooked:
> @Rabit: Under penalty of perjury, where were you on the night of January 18, 1986, 9pm?

Wow. That day. I remember it well – much to my frustration.

But 9pm, well, by that point most of it was over. The sun had been set for a couple hours, but we couldn’t tell; the clouds and rain were so dark, it might as well have been night all day. The rain just never let up that day. Turned out to be a good thing, though, as it washed away all the... Well, you wanted me to focus on 9pm.

By that point, I’d taken care of everything that needed to be done, cleaned up the “mess”, so-to-speak. But the guys, they’d only been there a little over an hour. They’d come over to do some violence, and I was generally up for that. We had rules to stick to, though. No raping – we didn’t go in for that kind of action – but burning down buildings was definitely on the menu for the evening. (Teenagers in small towns: You just never know what they’ll do when they get bored.)

It was long ago, so what we were doing at exactly 9 is a little fuzzy. I believe Eric had already offed that annoying gal who’d been pestering him for weeks, and they were already lighting her place up to cover the evidence. I was frustrated, as I knew there were better things we could be doing. But this was what they wanted, to spread mayhem and discord. It was silly, looking back on it now, not stopping them, not getting them to realize the consequences of their actions. But then it was just easier to go along with it.

Bob... Well, Bob was being Bob. I mean seriously, the point was to just burn the building down and get away, right? Just to try to keep anyone from realizing what had happened.

He really didn’t need to throw that fireball.

I mean, at that point, he destroyed half the buildings around her place, which started a fire that nearly took out the entire village, and since most were asleep when it first started a lot of them died in the ensuing insanity. (Unfortunately, it wasn’t raining in game like it was in the real world. That would have helped reduce the damage immensely.)

I’d spent a lot of time creating those NPCs, and they just killed them off without thought!

Just ridiculously frustrating...

 

So yeah, that was what I was doing on the night of January 18, 1986, at 9pm: In the middle of an AD&D game (1st Ed before it was 1st Ed) in my original game world of Maerson (after spending a day outside – in the rain – doing yard work) at our place in rural western Washington.

![](upload://v3ihd5sp0VEeWZIPn4SqA03Rdmb.gif)

(FYI: January 18, 1986, is still on the books as tied for the 7th highest rainfall for Seattle.)

posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
Honestly, any Dragon that kidnaps my wife is in trouble.  I would just steer clear and wait for that poor Dragon to bring her back.  She's an amazing woman, but you don't cross her without regretting it.

If she had to be rescued, I'd chop up the pancreas with the sharpened edge of the Runcible spoon, then mix that in with the Baked beans, and place that outside the Dragon's cave.  When the smell of such delicacies wafted into the cave and the Dragon came out to investigate he would be a spoon short of a delicious meal.  At that point I would have Redeemer Fanatic offer to trade him the spoon for my wife, he would obviously decline, as the quality of her pies would far outweigh the tasty treat in front of him.  At that point I would break down into tears, beg and plead, and the dragon, annoyed, would knock me over and take the spoon by force.  Alas, the Dragon and spoon both being fanciful creations of the imagination would violate the Learian principle of imaginary constructs and merge into one hideous sliced Quince eating mass.

All that would be left to do is have Redeemer fanatic save Dr. Lucky and for me to use the sharpened edge of the Dragon Spoon to cut my true love free, at which point she would throw herself into my arms, tell me how manly I am and ask me to make her a sandwich.

One mince and sliced quince sandwich (without pickles, that would be ridiculous) later the story ends.

posts.name: Pydro
posts.cooked:
I know. *hangs head in shame*

My favorite mythological creature, I haven't really thought of it before. So, I decided to take a slighly different approach. Which type of creature would I like to enslave. Now, I am not really interested in world domination, so no dragons or any such thing. I just want soemtihng to do my manual labor for me, but I want a little bit of inherent magic, so no dwarves or any such thing. I also would like something that would make me laugh. So I am thinking that my favorite creature to enslave would be a fairy. They have a human body, to make things easier to do, and they have the right mixture of wimsical and mischievous to keep me entertained. (Does anyone know if they keep these qualities when they are enslaved?)

 

On that note, I will include my favorite piece of advice regarding mythological creatures:

"Never play leap-frog with a unicorn."

@Theta_Sigma: Kittens, puppies or bunnies? Why?

posts.name: Theta_Sigma
posts.cooked:
For a long time when I was growing up, the only pets we had at home were a number of goldfish, usually two at a time. As cute as they are, it's hard to get attached to goldfish.

 

This changed when the neighbour's cat decided it was going to start hunting and bringing it's prey home. We were having dinner one night, when there was a knock at the door. The family on the other side of the neighbours had caught the cat getting into their rabbit hutch and making off with one of the baby bunnies, and they'd seen it come into our yard. After searching in the dark, we managed to find the poor thing (thankfully alive and unharmed, it had just been dropped in the grass) and they took it home. A few weeks later, the cat dropped another one in our yard. It was a little bigger, but it was about the same age as the other rabbits were. We managed to get the cat to drop it, and took it to the rabbit-owning family. This one was not theirs, and it would be hugely irresponsible to let it out, so we kept him.

 

Since then, we've had a number of rabbits, and each one has shown that they are intelligent creatures, each with unique personalities. I've never seen personalities show so clearly in any other animal (except humans).

 

So yeah, bunnies. But not just cos they're cute. Which they are.
